title: Contractual link and unlink semantics - non-invasive and reversible
description: WHY: linking must be safe to run against any checkout including someone elses - it is a machine-local registry fact, not a project mutation - and unlink must never destroy history or strand references. WHAT: (1) bwrk global link <path> validates the target is a Boreal workspace; when uninitialized it offers bwrk init interactively or via an --init flag, registers the entry (using the stable id from the sibling task), and backfills an initial rollup placeholder; assert with a test that link performs zero writes inside the target repo directory. (2) bwrk global unlink <project-id> soft-archives by default (lifecycle archived, rollup refresh stops, boards hide it) and --purge removes the entry entirely with a confirmation prompt; neither variant touches project data. (3) Document the semantics in the design doc and docs/cli/COMMANDS.md. Depends on stable ids and lifecycle states.
acceptanceCriteria: Link against a fresh non-Boreal directory offers init and registers on acceptance; a test asserts no file inside the target repo changed during link of an existing workspace
Unlink default archives and --purge removes, both covered by tests, neither modifying project data
